name: Tawitawi Brown-Dove
rangeDescription: Tawitawi (sulu archipelago)
description: A medium-sized dove of lowland secondary forest on Tawi-Tawi Island, where it is the only brown-dove. Dark brown above with a gray head, purplish iridescence on the back of the neck, rufous-brown underparts from the throat to the belly, white under the base of the tail, and a pale gray tail tip.

name: Black-banded Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: North-central australia (western escarpment of arnhem land)
description: Very large black-and-white forest pigeon, found as singles or small groups in large fruiting trees beside sandstone escarpments in the Kakadu National Park region of the Northern Territory. Generally hard to find.

name: Shovel-billed Kookaburra
rangeDescription: New guinea (primarily in hills and adjacent lowlands)
description: A huge, rare kingfisher of rainforest interior from lowlands to mid-mountains. Its unnaturally large bill makes it look almost unrecognisable as a kingfisher.

name: Sulawesi Lilac Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Sulawesi and lembeh island
description: A unique forest kingfisher. Largely pale brown with an eye-catching red bill, a prominent dark mask with pale flecks on its upper border, dark wings, and a rufous tail.

name: Green Warbler
rangeDescription: Caucasus to northern türkiye, northern iran, and northwestern afghanistan; winters southern india
description: Nondescript leaf warbler with two whitish wing bars (often only one visible), dull to bright greenish upperparts, a yellow wash usually restricted to the face, and a pale orange lower bill. Breeds in forest in the Caucasus mountains.

name: Snowy-throated Babbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of northeastern india (northeastern assam and southeastern arunachal pradesh)
description: A small, dark brown bird with a contrastingly black-and-white face. The black cheeks are sandwiched between a long, thick white eyebrow and a white throat.

name: Graceful Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Southern new guinea, including aru islands (off southwestern new guinea), southern torres strait islands, and cape york peninsula
description: A small olive-gray honeyeater with a circular pale yellow cheek patch and a relatively fine bill. Can be confused with Lewin’s Honeyeater and Yellow-spotted Honeyeater, but note the shape of the cheek patch: crescent-shaped on Lewin’s Honeyeater and oval on Yellow-spotted Honeyeater.

name: Wahlberg's Eagle
rangeDescription: Savanna of sub-saharan africa
description: A small brown eagle with a slighter head and weaker beak than in larger brown eagles. A short crest gives the head a distinct squared-off look.

name: Patagonian Tinamou
rangeDescription: Savanna of southwestern argentina and southern chile
description: Large, cryptically patterned chickenlike bird of Patagonian grasslands with bushes and low shrubs. Scarce and rarely encountered.

name: Urrao Antpitta
rangeDescription: Northern part of western andes of colombia (antioquia)
description: This antpitta has a very small range in the northern part of Colombia’s western Andes. It was described to science in 2010 and is considered highly endangered.

name: Empress Brilliant
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of southwestern colombia to northwestern ecuador
description: Impressive hummingbird of Andean cloud forest in northwestern Ecuador and western Colombia. Large, thick-billed, and long-tailed, with golden sheen on the belly.

name: Snowy-crowned Tern
rangeDescription: Lagoons and marshes of southeastern brazil and uruguay to patagonia
description: Attractive but often rather local tern of southern South America. Favors shallow coastal waters, but also ranges inland locally along rivers and lakes.

name: Plain-pouched Hornbill
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar, southwestern and southern thailand, and northern thai-malay peninsula
description: Medium-sized hornbill; resembles a smaller version of Wreathed Hornbill. Black with a white tail.

name: Madagascar Jacana
rangeDescription: Lakes, ponds, and marshes of madagascar
description: Distinctive shape that is typical of jacanas, including enormous feet. Most adults have white on the back of the head and neck, though some are completely dark-headed.

name: Bachman's Warbler
rangeDescription: Formerly southeastern usa; wintered to cuba and bahamas (probably extinct)
description: Jewel of a warbler, probably extinct. Male is distinctive, with a black patch on the lower throat and chest.

name: Golden Bowerbird
rangeDescription: Highland rain forest of northeastern australia (northeastern queensland)
description: Small bowerbird restricted to higher-elevation rainforest in Northern Queensland. Male has stunning bright yellow underparts, yellowish-brown face, and dull yellowish back.

name: Pygmy Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: High montane forest of northern, central, and southeastern sulawesi
description: A distinctive small cuckooshrike with bright white underbody, a dusky gray upperside, and a prominent red eye. Males display a contrasting black face and chin, while females’ faces have the same gray color as the back.

name: Yellow-plumed Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Mallee of southern australia (southwestern western australia to central new south wales)
description: Adult birds primarily olive-brown with heavy gray streaking on the underparts. Named after its long, yellow neck feathers.

name: American White Pelican
rangeDescription: Breeds inland south-central british columbia and northeastern alberta to west-central ontario (southwestern and south-central canada) southward to central california and texas (southwestern to south-central usa); non-breeders range inland southern usa to northwestern central america
description: Extremely large and conspicuous. White with black wingtips.

name: Kashmir Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Himalayas of northern india (kashmir); winters to southern india and sri lanka
description: Stubby little flycatcher with a highly restricted range; breeds in a corner of the northwestern Himalayas and winters in isolated pockets of hill forest in southern India and Sri Lanka. Male is gray above and bright orange below; female is paler, with only a faint orange wash on the chest.
